children.name: Melursus
children.description: Melursus — a genus of bears in the family Ursidae.

children.name: Melursus ursinus
children.description: The sloth bear, also known as the Indian bear, is a myrmecophagous bear species native to the Indian subcontinent. It feeds on fruits, ants and termites. It is listed as vulnerable on the IUCN Red List, mainly because of habitat loss and degradation.

children.name: Ailuropoda
children.description: Ailuropoda — a genus of bears in the family Ursidae.

children.name: Ailuropoda melanoleuca
children.description: The giant panda, also known as the panda bear or simply panda, is a bear species endemic to China. It is characterised by its white coat with black patches around the eyes, ears, legs and shoulders. Its body is rotund; adult individuals weigh 100 to 115 kg and are typically 1.2 to 1.9 m long.

children.name: Ailuropoda microta
children.description: Ailuropoda microta is the earliest known member of the genus Ailuropoda, which includes the living giant panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca).

children.name: Tremarctos
children.description: Tremarctos — a genus of bears in the family Ursidae.

children.name: Tremarctos ornatus
children.description: The spectacled bear, also known as the Andean bear, is a species of bear native to the Andes Mountains in northern and western South America. It is the only living species of bear native to South America, and the last remaining short-faced bear. Unlike other omnivorous bears, the diet of the spectacled bear is mostly herbivorous.

children.name: Helarctos
children.description: Helarctos — a genus of bears in the family Ursidae.

children.name: Helarctos malayanus
children.description: The sun bear is a bear species in the family Ursidae found in the tropical forests of Southeast Asia. It is the only species in the genus Helarctos and the smallest bear species, standing nearly 70 cm (28 in) at the shoulder and weighing 25–65 kg (55–143 lb). It is stockily built, with large paws, strongly curved claws, small, rounded ears and a short snout.

children.name: Ursus
children.description: Ursus — a genus of bears in the family Ursidae.

children.name: Ursus abstrusus
children.description: Protarctos is an extinct genus of basal ursine bear that lived in North America and Eurasia during the Pliocene and into Early Pleistocene.

children.name: Ursus americanus
children.description: The American black bear, or simply black bear, is a species of medium-sized bear which is endemic to North America. It is the continent's smallest and most widely distributed bear species. It is an omnivore, with a diet varying greatly depending on season and location.

children.name: Ursus arctos
children.description: The brown bear is a large bear native to Eurasia and North America. Of the land carnivorans, it is rivaled in size only by its closest relative, the polar bear, which is much less variable in size and slightly bigger on average. The brown bear is a sexually dimorphic species, as adult males are larger and more compactly built than females.

children.name: Ursus deningeri
children.description: Ursus deningeri (sometimes called Deninger's bear) is an extinct species of bear native to Eurasia from the late Early Pleistocene to the Middle Pleistocene.

children.name: Ursus etruscus
children.description: Ursus etruscus, the Etruscan bear, is an extinct bear species that was native to Eurasia during the Early Pleistocene, living from approximately 2.2 million to around 1.4–1.2 million years ago.

children.name: Ursus ingressus
children.description: Ursus ingressus is an extinct species of the cave bear species complex that lived in Central Europe during the Late Pleistocene.

children.name: Ursus maritimus
children.description: The polar bear is a large bear native to the Arctic and nearby areas. It is closely related to the brown bear, and the two species can interbreed. The polar bear is the largest extant species of bear and land carnivore by body mass, with adult males weighing 300–800 kg (660–1,760 lb).

children.name: Ursus minimus
children.description: Ursus minimus (the Auvergne bear) is an extinct species of bear, endemic to Europe during the Pliocene and Pleistocene, living from 5.3 to 1.8 Mya, existing for about .

children.description: The cave bear is a prehistoric species of bear that lived in Europe and Asia during the Pleistocene and became extinct about 24,000 years ago during the Last Glacial Maximum.

children.name: Ursus thibetanus
children.description: The Asian black bear (Ursus thibetanus), also known as the Asiatic black bear, moon bear and white-chested bear, is a medium-sized bear species native to Asia that is largely adapted to an arboreal lifestyle.
